title: Multimodal Dynamics in Early Triadic Interactions at Home: A Longitudinal Analysis Throughout Infants' First Year of Life
abstract: ABSTRACT Early communicative development during the first year of life unfolds through rich, multimodal exchanges in which infants and caregivers coordinate multiple resources—such as gestures, object use, vocalizations, and touch—into dynamic patterns that shape early language trajectories. However, less is known about how these behaviors evolve for both partners in triadic contexts, where objects anchor joint engagement, and how they are associated with language development. This longitudinal study followed nine infant‐caregiver dyads with monthly behavioral observations from 2 to 12 months during naturalistic free‐play interactions at home. We frame‐by‐frame coded infant behaviors (spontaneous movements, rhythmic movements, gestures, vocalizations) and adult behaviors (distal object‐use demonstrations of varying complexity, rhythmic and non‐rhythmic touch). Analyses examined age‐related change, multimodal combinations, and their associations with MacArthur‐Bates CDI comprehension and production trajectories, assessed at 9, 12, and 16 months. Infants showed a decline in spontaneous movements across the first year, while vocalizations were more often produced in isolation than alongside manual gestures. Multimodal combinations involving rhythmic movements with objects increased over time, whereas gesture‐vocalization combinations remained rare and did not show significant age‐related increases. In adults, simple object‐use demonstrations decreased, whereas more complex demonstrations and non‐rhythmic touch became relatively more prominent, although both proximal and distal interaction strategies decreased overall with age. Certain adult behaviors—particularly symbolic object‐use demonstrations—were associated with infants' language‐growth trajectories. Several infant behavioral trajectories were also associated with language growth, with these associations varying as a function of estimated language level at 12.3 months. These findings reveal intertwined infant‐caregiver developmental trajectories and underscore that early communication in triadic contexts relies on coordinated motor, vocal, and material channels sustained by shared engagement with objects.
